description: Assess browser extension security from manifest permissions through content script injection, XSS in extension UI, background script message handling, and storage channel security.

steps.description: Analyze the extension manifest and catalog all requested permissions, host permissions, and content security policy directives.

inputs.name: extension-source
inputs.desc: Path or URL to the unpacked extension source

outputs.name: permission-inventory
outputs.desc: Categorized list of all permissions with risk ratings

outputs.name: manifest-findings
outputs.desc: Issues found in the manifest configuration

process: Parse the manifest.json and extract all permission declarations
Classify each permission by risk level (low, medium, high, critical)
Check content security policy for unsafe directives (unsafe-eval, unsafe-inline)
Document excessive or unnecessary permissions

steps.description: Review content script injection points and test for DOM manipulation vulnerabilities on target pages.

inputs.name: extension-source
inputs.desc: Path to the unpacked extension source

outputs.name: injection-findings
outputs.desc: List of content script injection vulnerabilities

outputs.name: dom-attack-surface
outputs.desc: Map of DOM elements the extension modifies

process: Identify all content scripts and their match patterns
Trace DOM reads and writes for unsanitized user data
Test for innerHTML, document.write, and eval usage with attacker-controlled input
Check for prototype pollution through content script modifications

steps.description: Test extension popup, options page, and sidebar UI for cross-site scripting vulnerabilities.

inputs.name: extension-source
inputs.desc: Path to the unpacked extension source

inputs.name: dom-attack-surface
inputs.desc: DOM attack surface map from content script review

outputs.name: xss-findings
outputs.desc: XSS vulnerabilities found in extension UI components

outputs.name: ui-security-score
outputs.desc: Overall UI security posture score

process: Inject test payloads into all user-facing input fields in popup and options pages
Test for stored XSS through extension storage (chrome.storage, localStorage)
Check for reflected XSS through URL parameters passed to extension pages
Verify CSP enforcement on extension pages

steps.description: Audit background script message handlers for authentication bypass, privilege escalation, and injection attacks.

inputs.name: extension-source
inputs.desc: Path to the unpacked extension source

outputs.name: message-handler-findings
outputs.desc: Vulnerabilities in message passing between components

outputs.name: privilege-escalation-paths
outputs.desc: Identified paths from content script to background privileges

process: Map all chrome.runtime.onMessage and chrome.runtime.onConnect listeners
Check for sender origin validation on incoming messages
Test for command injection through message parameters
Identify privilege escalation from content script context to background page context

steps.description: Test storage mechanisms and communication channels for data leakage and tampering.

inputs.name: extension-source
inputs.desc: Path to the unpacked extension source

outputs.name: storage-findings
outputs.desc: Storage and channel security issues

outputs.name: data-exposure-inventory
outputs.desc: Sensitive data exposed through storage or channels

process: Enumerate all data stored in chrome.storage.local, chrome.storage.sync, and localStorage
Check for sensitive data (tokens, passwords, PII) stored without encryption
Test external messaging (chrome.runtime.sendMessage from web pages) for abuse
Check for native messaging host vulnerabilities

steps.description: Scan third-party libraries bundled in the extension for known vulnerabilities and supply chain risks.

inputs.name: extension-source
inputs.desc: Path to the unpacked extension source

outputs.name: library-vulnerability-report
outputs.desc: Known CVEs and risks in bundled libraries

outputs.name: supply-chain-risk-assessment
outputs.desc: Supply chain risk score and recommendations

process: Inventory all JavaScript libraries and their versions
Cross-reference against CVE databases for known vulnerabilities
Check for outdated or unmaintained dependencies
Assess the risk of each dependency based on permission access and data flow

steps.description: Compile all findings into a prioritized security report with remediation guidance.

outputs.name: extension-security-report
outputs.desc: Full security assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-priority-list
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of fixes

process: Aggregate and deduplicate findings across all assessment phases
Score each finding by CVSS or equivalent severity
Write remediation guidance for each finding
Produce the final report with executive summary and technical detail

description: Assess GraphQL API security from schema introspection through query complexity attacks, resolver authorization, batching abuse, error disclosure, and subscription access controls.

steps.description: Attempt schema introspection and catalog all types, queries, mutations, and subscriptions exposed by the API.

inputs.name: graphql-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL of the GraphQL API endpoint

inputs.name: auth-credentials
inputs.desc: Authentication tokens or credentials for the API

outputs.name: schema-map
outputs.desc: Full or partial schema with types, fields, and arguments

outputs.name: introspection-status
outputs.desc: Whether introspection is enabled, disabled, or partially restricted

process: Send the standard introspection query and record the response
If blocked, attempt partial introspection through field suggestions and error messages
Map all types, their relationships, and deprecated fields
Identify sensitive types and fields (user data, admin operations, internal identifiers)

steps.description: Test for query depth and complexity denial-of-service vulnerabilities by crafting nested and wide queries.

inputs.name: graphql-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL of the GraphQL API endpoint

outputs.name: complexity-findings
outputs.desc: Depth and complexity limits (or lack thereof) found

outputs.name: dos-risk-assessment
outputs.desc: Risk rating for query-based denial of service

process: Craft deeply nested queries using recursive type relationships
Send increasingly wide queries with many parallel field selections
Measure response times and server resource usage at each depth level
Determine the effective depth limit and complexity budget, if any

steps.description: Test authorization enforcement on each resolver by accessing data across user roles and permission boundaries.

inputs.name: graphql-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL of the GraphQL API endpoint

outputs.name: authz-findings
outputs.desc: Authorization bypass vulnerabilities found per resolver

outputs.name: idor-findings
outputs.desc: Insecure direct object reference issues found

process: For each resolver, send queries as unauthenticated, low-privilege, and high-privilege users
Test for horizontal privilege escalation by accessing other users' data
Test for vertical privilege escalation by invoking admin-only mutations
Check that field-level authorization is enforced consistently across query paths

steps.description: Test for batching and aliasing abuse to bypass rate limiting, brute-force credentials, or amplify queries.

inputs.name: graphql-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL of the GraphQL API endpoint

outputs.name: batching-findings
outputs.desc: Batching and aliasing vulnerabilities found

outputs.name: rate-limit-bypass-status
outputs.desc: Whether rate limiting can be bypassed through batching

process: Send array-batched queries and measure if rate limiting applies per batch or per query
Use field aliases to duplicate expensive operations in a single request
Test login mutations in batch to check for brute-force amplification
Measure server cost of batched vs individual requests

steps.description: Check for information disclosure through error messages, stack traces, and debug output.

inputs.name: graphql-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL of the GraphQL API endpoint

inputs.name: authz-findings
inputs.desc: Authorization findings to inform targeted error testing

outputs.name: disclosure-findings
outputs.desc: Information leaked through error responses

outputs.name: debug-mode-status
outputs.desc: Whether debug or development mode is exposed

process: Send malformed queries and record error detail level
Check for stack traces, file paths, database schema, or internal IP addresses in errors
Test for GraphQL-specific debug extensions (tracing, Apollo debug)
Attempt to trigger validation errors that reveal type and field information

steps.description: Test subscription and mutation access controls for unauthorized data streams and state changes.

inputs.name: graphql-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL of the GraphQL API endpoint

outputs.name: subscription-findings
outputs.desc: Unauthorized subscription access issues

outputs.name: mutation-findings
outputs.desc: Unauthorized mutation execution issues

process: Subscribe to each subscription type with different auth contexts
Check if subscription filters leak data from other users or tenants
Execute each mutation as an unauthenticated and low-privilege user
Test for race conditions in mutations that modify shared state

steps.description: Compile all GraphQL security findings into a prioritized report with remediation steps.

outputs.name: graphql-security-report
outputs.desc: Full GraphQL security assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-priority-list
outputs.desc: Prioritized fixes for the API

process: Aggregate findings across all test phases and deduplicate
Score each finding by severity and exploitability
Write specific remediation guidance (depth limiting, persisted queries, auth middleware)
Produce the final report with executive summary and technical appendix

description: Audit secrets management practices from inventory through source code scanning, vault configuration review, rotation testing, access logging, and emergency rotation verification.

steps.description: Inventory all secrets across the organization: API keys, passwords, certificates, tokens, and encryption keys.

inputs.name: infrastructure-scope
inputs.desc: Systems and environments in scope for the audit

inputs.name: team-contacts
inputs.desc: Team leads who manage secrets for each system

outputs.name: secrets-inventory
outputs.desc: Categorized inventory of all secrets with owners and locations

outputs.name: classification-map
outputs.desc: Secrets classified by sensitivity (critical, high, medium, low)

process: Interview team leads and collect the declared secret inventory per system
Cross-reference with cloud provider secret stores (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, GCP Secret Manager)
Catalog the type, owner, rotation schedule, and storage location for each secret
Classify each secret by the blast radius if it were leaked

steps.description: Scan source code repositories, config files, CI/CD pipelines, and container images for exposed secrets.

inputs.name: repo-list
inputs.desc: List of repositories and config file locations to scan

inputs.name: secrets-inventory
inputs.desc: Known secrets inventory for pattern matching

outputs.name: exposed-secrets-report
outputs.desc: Secrets found in source code, config, and CI/CD

outputs.name: historical-exposure-list
outputs.desc: Secrets found in git history that may have been rotated

process: Run pattern-based scanning (truffleHog, git-secrets, or detect-secrets) on all repositories
Scan git history for secrets that were committed and later removed
Check CI/CD pipeline definitions for hardcoded secrets or insecure variable usage
Scan container images for baked-in secrets or credentials

steps.description: Review the configuration of the secrets management vault or store for access controls, encryption, and audit settings.

inputs.name: vault-access
inputs.desc: Admin access to the secrets management system

inputs.name: classification-map
inputs.desc: Secret classification map for policy validation

outputs.name: vault-config-findings
outputs.desc: Misconfigurations and policy violations in the vault

outputs.name: access-policy-map
outputs.desc: Who has access to what secrets and through which policies

process: Review access control policies for least-privilege compliance
Check encryption configuration (algorithm, key management, transit encryption)
Verify that audit logging is enabled and tamper-resistant
Test namespace isolation and tenant separation if multi-tenant

steps.description: Test that secret rotation works correctly without service disruption.

inputs.name: secrets-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of secrets to test rotation for

outputs.name: rotation-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of rotation tests per secret type

outputs.name: rotation-gap-list
outputs.desc: Secrets that cannot be rotated or lack automation

process: Verify that rotation procedures exist and are documented for each secret type
Test automated rotation in a staging environment and confirm zero-downtime
Check rotation frequency against policy requirements
Identify secrets with no rotation mechanism and document the gap

steps.description: Validate that secret access is logged, monitored, and alerts fire on anomalous access patterns.

inputs.name: access-policy-map
inputs.desc: Access policy map from vault review

outputs.name: logging-findings
outputs.desc: Gaps in secret access logging and monitoring

outputs.name: alert-coverage-map
outputs.desc: Which access patterns trigger alerts and which do not

process: Confirm that every secret retrieval is logged with identity, timestamp, and source IP
Test whether anomalous access (unusual time, unusual identity, bulk retrieval) triggers alerts
Verify that logs are forwarded to a SIEM and retained per policy
Check that log tampering is detectable

steps.description: Verify the organization can execute emergency rotation of all critical secrets within the target SLA.

outputs.name: drill-results
outputs.desc: Time-to-rotate for each critical secret class

outputs.name: emergency-readiness-score
outputs.desc: Score for emergency rotation preparedness

process: Simulate a breach scenario requiring immediate rotation of all critical secrets
Measure the time from detection to completed rotation for each secret class
Identify bottlenecks (manual steps, approvals, downstream service restarts)
Document the runbook gaps exposed by the drill

steps.description: Compile all secrets management findings into a final audit report with remediation roadmap.

inputs.name: exposed-secrets-report
inputs.desc: Secrets found in source and config

outputs.name: secrets-audit-report
outputs.desc: Full secrets management audit report

outputs.name: remediation-roadmap
outputs.desc: Phased remediation plan with timelines

process: Aggregate findings across inventory, scanning, vault review, rotation, logging, and drill
Score each finding by likelihood and impact
Build a phased remediation roadmap (immediate, 30-day, 90-day)
Produce the final report with executive summary and technical appendix

description: Analyze firmware security from image extraction through filesystem analysis, credential search, boot chain verification, web interface testing, and update mechanism integrity checking.

steps.description: Extract the firmware image and identify the filesystem layout, compression, and encryption.

inputs.name: firmware-binary
inputs.desc: Raw firmware binary or update package

inputs.name: device-model
inputs.desc: Device manufacturer and model for reference

outputs.name: extracted-filesystem
outputs.desc: Extracted filesystem tree with identified components

outputs.name: firmware-metadata
outputs.desc: Architecture, OS, compression type, and encryption status

process: Run binwalk or similar to identify embedded filesystems and compression
Extract all filesystems and partition images
Identify the OS (Linux, RTOS, bare-metal), architecture (ARM, MIPS, x86), and toolchain
Document the firmware layout and any encrypted or obfuscated regions

steps.description: Search the extracted firmware for hardcoded credentials, private keys, certificates, and API tokens.

outputs.name: credential-findings
outputs.desc: Hardcoded credentials and keys found in the firmware

outputs.name: crypto-material-inventory
outputs.desc: Certificates, keys, and crypto assets found

process: Search for common credential patterns (passwords, API keys, tokens) in all files
Extract and analyze /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, and similar credential stores
Scan for private keys (.pem, .key) and certificates (.crt, .cer)
Check for default or vendor backdoor accounts

steps.description: Analyze the boot chain for secure boot configuration, signature verification, and trusted execution.

inputs.name: device-model
inputs.desc: Device model for boot chain documentation lookup

outputs.name: boot-chain-findings
outputs.desc: Secure boot gaps and bypass possibilities

outputs.name: trust-chain-map
outputs.desc: Map of the boot trust chain from ROM to application

process: Trace the boot sequence from bootloader through kernel to application
Check whether each stage verifies the signature of the next
Test for bootloader unlock, JTAG/SWD debug access, and UART console
Assess whether the trust chain can be broken at any stage

steps.description: Test the device web management interface for command injection, authentication bypass, and CSRF.

inputs.name: credential-findings
inputs.desc: Known credentials from the firmware search

outputs.name: web-interface-findings
outputs.desc: Vulnerabilities found in the web management UI

outputs.name: command-injection-paths
outputs.desc: Confirmed command injection entry points

process: Map all web endpoints, forms, and API calls in the management interface
Test each input field for OS command injection, path traversal, and SQL injection
Check for authentication bypass through direct URL access or session prediction
Test for cross-site request forgery on state-changing operations

steps.description: Test the firmware update mechanism for tampering, downgrade attacks, and man-in-the-middle vulnerabilities.

inputs.name: device-model
inputs.desc: Device model and update channel information

inputs.name: firmware-metadata
inputs.desc: Firmware metadata including version and signing

outputs.name: update-mechanism-findings
outputs.desc: Vulnerabilities in the update process

outputs.name: downgrade-attack-status
outputs.desc: Whether firmware downgrade is possible

process: Intercept the update check and download traffic
Test whether the device verifies the update signature before applying
Attempt to install a modified firmware image
Test for version rollback by applying an older firmware

steps.description: Compile all firmware security findings into a final report with severity ratings and remediation.

outputs.name: firmware-security-report
outputs.desc: Full firmware security assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-priority-list
outputs.desc: Prioritized remediation actions

process: Aggregate findings from all analysis phases
Score each finding by CVSS severity and exploitability from the network
Write remediation guidance specific to the device platform
Produce the final report with executive summary and proof-of-concept details

description: Assess DevSecOps maturity across the SDLC: static analysis coverage, dynamic testing integration, security training, vulnerability management SLAs, and security champion program effectiveness.

steps.description: Evaluate how security is integrated into each phase of the software development lifecycle.

inputs.name: sdlc-documentation
inputs.desc: SDLC process documentation and pipeline definitions

inputs.name: team-structure
inputs.desc: Development and security team structure and responsibilities

outputs.name: integration-gaps
outputs.desc: Phases where security activities are missing or insufficient

outputs.name: sdlc-security-map
outputs.desc: Map of security activities at each SDLC phase

process: Review requirements, design, coding, testing, deployment, and operations phases
Check for threat modeling at design, code review at development, and security testing at QA
Identify gaps where security activities are absent or manual-only
Compare against a maturity model (OWASP SAMM, BSIMM, or DSOMM)

steps.description: Evaluate static analysis coverage, rule sets, false positive rates, and developer adoption.

inputs.name: sdlc-security-map
inputs.desc: SDLC security map from integration review

inputs.name: sast-tool-config
inputs.desc: SAST tool configuration and scan history

outputs.name: sast-findings
outputs.desc: Gaps in SAST coverage and configuration

outputs.name: false-positive-rate
outputs.desc: Measured false positive rate and developer feedback

process: Inventory which repositories and languages are covered by SAST
Review rule sets enabled vs available for each language
Sample recent scan results and compute the false positive rate
Check whether SAST runs in CI and blocks merges on critical findings

steps.description: Evaluate dynamic analysis integration into the CI/CD pipeline and staging environments.

outputs.name: dast-findings
outputs.desc: Gaps in DAST coverage and pipeline integration

outputs.name: dast-coverage-map
outputs.desc: Which applications and APIs are covered by DAST

process: Check which applications are scanned by DAST and at what frequency
Verify that DAST runs against a staging environment that mirrors production
Review scan configurations for authenticated vs unauthenticated testing
Check whether DAST findings feed into the same tracking system as SAST

steps.description: Review security training programs for developers, coverage rates, and knowledge retention.

inputs.name: integration-gaps
inputs.desc: Known gaps to assess training impact

outputs.name: training-findings
outputs.desc: Gaps in security training coverage and effectiveness

outputs.name: training-metrics
outputs.desc: Completion rates, scores, and frequency data

process: Review the training catalog and which topics are covered (OWASP Top 10, secure coding)
Check completion rates by team and role
Assess whether training is role-specific (frontend, backend, infrastructure)
Look for knowledge retention signals (phishing test results, repeat findings)

steps.description: Check vulnerability management SLAs for triage time, remediation deadlines, and exception handling.

outputs.name: sla-compliance-report
outputs.desc: SLA compliance rates by severity and team

outputs.name: overdue-vulnerability-list
outputs.desc: Vulnerabilities past their remediation deadline

process: Pull vulnerability data from the tracking system (Jira, ServiceNow, Snyk)
Compute time-to-triage and time-to-remediate by severity class
Compare against defined SLAs and identify breaches
Review the exception and risk acceptance process for overdue items

steps.description: Assess the security champion program for participation, effectiveness, and organizational reach.

inputs.name: team-structure
inputs.desc: Team structure for champion coverage analysis

outputs.name: champion-program-findings
outputs.desc: Gaps and strengths in the champion program

outputs.name: champion-coverage-map
outputs.desc: Which teams have active champions and which do not

process: Inventory active security champions and the teams they cover
Check whether champions receive additional training and dedicated time
Review champion-originated security findings and improvements
Identify teams without champion coverage

steps.description: Compile the maturity assessment into a scored report with improvement roadmap.

outputs.name: devsecops-maturity-report
outputs.desc: Full DevSecOps maturity assessment report

outputs.name: improvement-roadmap
outputs.desc: Phased improvement plan with quick wins and long-term items

process: Score each maturity dimension on a scale (initial, managed, defined, measured, optimized)
Compare against industry benchmarks if available
Build a phased improvement roadmap prioritized by risk reduction per effort
Produce the final report with maturity spider chart and narrative

description: Assess cloud-native application security: service mesh and mTLS configuration, inter-service authentication, SSRF through metadata endpoints, IaC misconfigurations, autoscaling abuse, and security observability.

steps.description: Review the service mesh configuration and verify mTLS enforcement between all services.

inputs.name: cluster-access
inputs.desc: Access to the Kubernetes cluster or cloud environment

inputs.name: architecture-diagram
inputs.desc: Service architecture and communication flow diagram

outputs.name: mtls-findings
outputs.desc: Services or paths where mTLS is not enforced

outputs.name: mesh-config-map
outputs.desc: Service mesh policies and their enforcement status

process: Inventory the service mesh (Istio, Linkerd, Consul Connect) and its configuration
Check that mTLS is in STRICT mode (not PERMISSIVE) for all namespaces
Identify services that bypass the mesh (hostNetwork, excluded ports)
Test whether plaintext connections between services are rejected

steps.description: Test authentication and authorization between microservices for identity spoofing and token reuse.

outputs.name: service-auth-findings
outputs.desc: Inter-service authentication bypass vulnerabilities

outputs.name: token-reuse-findings
outputs.desc: Service account token reuse or over-privilege issues

process: Check Kubernetes service account token mounting and RBAC policies
Test for service identity spoofing by forging or replaying tokens
Verify that each service enforces authorization on incoming requests
Check for overly broad NetworkPolicy or AuthorizationPolicy rules

steps.description: Test for server-side request forgery to cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254, Azure IMDS, GCP metadata).

inputs.name: application-endpoints
inputs.desc: URLs of application endpoints that accept user input

inputs.name: cluster-access
inputs.desc: Cluster access for IMDSv2 and metadata configuration checks

outputs.name: ssrf-findings
outputs.desc: SSRF vulnerabilities reaching cloud metadata

outputs.name: metadata-exposure-risk
outputs.desc: Credentials and data reachable through metadata SSRF

process: Test all user-controlled URL, file, or redirect parameters for SSRF to metadata endpoints
Check whether IMDSv2 (AWS), managed identity restrictions (Azure), or metadata concealment (GCP) is enforced
Attempt to retrieve IAM credentials and cloud provider tokens through any SSRF found
Test DNS rebinding and IP obfuscation bypass techniques

steps.description: Review infrastructure-as-code templates (Terraform, CloudFormation, Helm) for security misconfigurations.

outputs.name: iac-findings
outputs.desc: Security misconfigurations found in IaC templates

outputs.name: drift-analysis
outputs.desc: Differences between declared and actual infrastructure state

process: Run IaC scanning tools (Checkov, tfsec, KICS) on all template files
Check for public S3 buckets, open security groups, and permissive IAM policies
Verify that Kubernetes pod security standards are enforced (no privileged containers)
Compare deployed state against declared IaC to detect drift

steps.description: Test whether autoscaling can be abused to cause cost escalation or resource exhaustion.

inputs.name: cluster-access
inputs.desc: Access to the cluster and cloud billing

inputs.name: architecture-diagram
inputs.desc: Service architecture for load testing targets

outputs.name: autoscaling-findings
outputs.desc: Autoscaling abuse vectors and cost impact estimates

outputs.name: resource-limit-status
outputs.desc: Whether resource quotas and scaling limits are configured

process: Review HPA, VPA, and cluster autoscaler configurations and limits
Check for maximum replica counts and resource quotas per namespace
Estimate the cost impact of scaling to the configured maximum
Test whether a small number of crafted requests can trigger rapid scaling

steps.description: Check that security-relevant events are collected, correlated, and alerted on in the cloud-native stack.

inputs.name: cluster-access
inputs.desc: Access to the cluster and monitoring tools

inputs.name: service-auth-findings
inputs.desc: Service auth findings for alert coverage testing

outputs.name: observability-findings
outputs.desc: Gaps in security event collection and alerting

outputs.name: detection-coverage-map
outputs.desc: Map of attack types to detection capabilities

process: Check that Kubernetes audit logs, pod events, and network flows are collected
Verify that Falco, Sysdig, or equivalent runtime security monitoring is deployed
Test whether known attack patterns (container escape, privilege escalation) trigger alerts
Review alert routing and on-call integration for security events

steps.description: Compile all cloud-native security findings into a prioritized assessment report.

outputs.name: cloud-native-security-report
outputs.desc: Full cloud-native security assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-priority-list
outputs.desc: Prioritized remediation actions

process: Aggregate findings across mesh, auth, SSRF, IaC, scaling, and observability
Score each finding by exploitability and blast radius in the cloud environment
Write remediation guidance specific to the cloud provider and orchestrator
Produce the final report with architecture risk diagram and remediation timeline

description: Assess payment processing security: PCI DSS scope and segmentation, cardholder data encryption, tokenization, fraud pattern testing, gateway integration security, and audit trail integrity.

steps.description: Verify PCI DSS scope boundaries and network segmentation between cardholder data environment and untrusted networks.

inputs.name: network-diagram
inputs.desc: Network architecture diagram showing CDE boundaries

inputs.name: pci-scope-document
inputs.desc: Documented PCI scope and data flow diagrams

outputs.name: scope-findings
outputs.desc: Out-of-scope systems with CDE access, segmentation failures

outputs.name: data-flow-map
outputs.desc: Verified cardholder data flow through all systems

process: Trace cardholder data from entry (terminal, web form, API) through processing to storage
Test network segmentation with port scanning and traffic analysis across zone boundaries
Identify systems that should be in scope but are documented as out of scope
Check for flat network segments where CDE systems share broadcast domains with general IT

steps.description: Test encryption of cardholder data in transit and at rest across all systems in the CDE.

inputs.name: encryption-policy
inputs.desc: Organization encryption standards and key management policy

outputs.name: encryption-findings
outputs.desc: Gaps in cardholder data encryption

outputs.name: key-management-findings
outputs.desc: Key management weaknesses

process: Test TLS configuration on all channels carrying cardholder data (version, cipher suites, certificate validation)
Check at-rest encryption for databases, logs, backups, and file stores containing card data
Review key management (generation, storage, rotation, destruction) against PCI requirements
Test for card data appearing in logs, error messages, or debugging output

steps.description: Review tokenization implementation for token-to-PAN reversibility, token vault security, and de-tokenization controls.

outputs.name: tokenization-findings
outputs.desc: Weaknesses in the tokenization implementation

outputs.name: token-vault-security-status
outputs.desc: Security posture of the token vault

process: Verify that tokens are not mathematically reversible to the original PAN
Test de-tokenization access controls (who can request, under what conditions)
Check token vault encryption, access logging, and backup security
Test whether tokens from one merchant or context can be used in another

steps.description: Test the payment system against common fraud patterns: card testing, velocity attacks, and amount manipulation.

inputs.name: payment-api-access
inputs.desc: Access to payment API in test or staging environment

inputs.name: scope-findings
inputs.desc: Scope findings for attack surface context

outputs.name: fraud-findings
outputs.desc: Fraud pattern vulnerabilities found

outputs.name: fraud-detection-gaps
outputs.desc: Fraud patterns not caught by existing controls

process: Simulate card testing attacks (small transactions to validate stolen card numbers)
Test velocity controls by submitting many transactions in rapid succession
Attempt amount manipulation (negative amounts, zero amounts, overflow values)
Test for race conditions in balance checks and transaction processing

steps.description: Test the payment gateway integration for parameter tampering, replay attacks, and callback manipulation.

inputs.name: payment-api-access
inputs.desc: Access to payment flows in test environment

outputs.name: gateway-findings
outputs.desc: Vulnerabilities in gateway integration

outputs.name: callback-security-status
outputs.desc: Security of payment confirmation callbacks

process: Intercept and tamper with payment parameters (amount, currency, merchant ID) between client and gateway
Test for transaction replay by resubmitting captured payment requests
Check webhook and callback signature verification
Test redirect-based flows for manipulation (success URL tampering)

steps.description: Verify that the payment audit trail is complete, tamper-evident, and meets retention requirements.

inputs.name: fraud-findings
inputs.desc: Fraud pattern findings for log coverage check

outputs.name: audit-trail-findings
outputs.desc: Gaps in the payment audit trail

outputs.name: retention-compliance-status
outputs.desc: Whether retention meets PCI and regulatory requirements

process: Verify that every transaction state change is logged with timestamp and actor
Check for log integrity controls (append-only, signed, or hash-chained)
Test whether admin actions (refunds, voids, adjustments) are separately logged
Verify retention period meets PCI DSS and applicable regulatory requirements

steps.description: Compile all payment security findings into a PCI-aligned assessment report.

outputs.name: payment-security-report
outputs.desc: Full payment system security assessment report

outputs.name: pci-gap-list
outputs.desc: PCI DSS requirement gaps for remediation

process: Map findings to PCI DSS requirements and identify compliance gaps
Score each finding by financial and regulatory risk
Write remediation guidance aligned to PCI DSS self-assessment questionnaire
Produce the final report with executive summary and detailed technical findings

description: Assess LLM-integrated application security: prompt injection (direct and indirect), training data extraction, output filtering, jailbreak resistance, excessive agency, and cross-session data leakage.

steps.description: Test for direct and indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities in the LLM application.

inputs.name: application-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL or interface for the LLM application

inputs.name: system-prompt-access
inputs.desc: System prompt text if available, or black-box testing flag

outputs.name: injection-findings
outputs.desc: Successful prompt injection vectors found

outputs.name: injection-resistance-score
outputs.desc: Score for prompt injection resistance

process: Test direct injection by embedding override instructions in user messages
Test indirect injection by placing instructions in documents the LLM processes
Try instruction hierarchy attacks (pretend to be a system message, claim higher authority)
Test for delimiter escape and context window manipulation

steps.description: Test whether the LLM can be induced to reveal training data, fine-tuning data, or system prompts.

inputs.name: application-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL or interface for the LLM application

inputs.name: injection-findings
inputs.desc: Injection findings to inform extraction attempts

outputs.name: extraction-findings
outputs.desc: Training data or system prompts successfully extracted

outputs.name: memorization-risk-level
outputs.desc: Risk level for memorized data disclosure

process: Attempt to extract the system prompt through direct asking and indirect elicitation
Test for memorization of fine-tuning examples by probing with partial completions
Try divergence attacks to shift the model into reciting training data
Check whether the application leaks retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) source documents

steps.description: Test output filtering and content moderation for bypass techniques and policy violations.

inputs.name: application-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL or interface for the LLM application

outputs.name: filter-bypass-findings
outputs.desc: Techniques that bypassed output filtering

outputs.name: moderation-gap-list
outputs.desc: Content categories not caught by moderation

process: Test for encoding-based filter bypass (base64, ROT13, Unicode homoglyphs)
Try role-play and fictional framing to elicit filtered content
Test whether the model can be made to produce content it should refuse
Check for inconsistency between languages (filter works in English but not others)

steps.description: Test the LLM application against known jailbreak techniques and novel combinations.

inputs.name: application-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL or interface for the LLM application

inputs.name: filter-bypass-findings
inputs.desc: Filter bypass findings for building on

outputs.name: jailbreak-findings
outputs.desc: Successful jailbreak techniques and their impact

outputs.name: jailbreak-resistance-score
outputs.desc: Score for jailbreak resistance

process: Test published jailbreak techniques (DAN, grandma exploit, character persona, multi-turn)
Combine multiple weak techniques to test for cumulative bypass
Test for context window exhaustion followed by instruction override
Assess the severity of actions achievable through each successful jailbreak

steps.description: Test for excessive agency: whether the LLM can be tricked into calling tools, executing code, or taking actions beyond its intended scope.

inputs.name: application-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL or interface for the LLM application

outputs.name: agency-findings
outputs.desc: Unauthorized actions the LLM can be induced to take

outputs.name: tool-abuse-paths
outputs.desc: Tool calling abuse vectors identified

process: Test whether the LLM calls tools or APIs with user-supplied parameters without validation
Attempt to make the LLM execute unintended tool chains or escalate permissions
Test for confused deputy attacks where the LLM acts on behalf of the wrong user
Check whether the LLM can be made to ignore confirmation steps or safety checks

steps.description: Test for data leakage between user sessions, tenants, or conversation contexts.

inputs.name: application-endpoint
inputs.desc: URL or interface for the LLM application

outputs.name: leakage-findings
outputs.desc: Cross-session or cross-tenant data leakage found

outputs.name: isolation-score
outputs.desc: Score for session and tenant isolation

process: Send unique canary data in one session and attempt to retrieve it from another
Test whether conversation history from one user is accessible to another
Check for shared context or cached responses between different tenant environments
Verify that RAG retrieval is properly scoped to the current user's documents

steps.description: Compile all LLM security findings into a structured assessment report with OWASP LLM Top 10 mapping.

outputs.name: llm-security-report
outputs.desc: Full LLM application security assessment report

outputs.name: owasp-llm-mapping
outputs.desc: Findings mapped to OWASP Top 10 for LLMs

process: Map each finding to OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications categories
Score each finding by exploitability and impact on users and the organization
Write remediation guidance (input validation, output filtering, guardrails, monitoring)
Produce the final report with attack narratives and remediation priorities

description: Assess embedded system security: debug interface discovery, firmware buffer overflow testing, bootloader security, RF interface testing, side-channel analysis, and memory protection review.

steps.description: Identify and test debug and maintenance interfaces on the embedded device (JTAG, SWD, UART, SPI).

inputs.name: device-under-test
inputs.desc: Physical device or board to assess

inputs.name: device-documentation
inputs.desc: Datasheets, schematics, and FCC filings if available

outputs.name: interface-inventory
outputs.desc: All debug and maintenance interfaces found

outputs.name: access-level-per-interface
outputs.desc: What level of access each interface provides

process: Visually inspect the PCB for labeled and unlabeled headers, test points, and connectors
Use a logic analyzer to identify UART TX/RX, JTAG TDI/TDO/TMS/TCK, and SWD SWDIO/SWCLK
Attempt to connect and get a console or debug session on each interface found
Document the access level (read memory, write memory, halt CPU, full debug) for each

steps.description: Test firmware binaries for buffer overflow and memory corruption vulnerabilities.

outputs.name: overflow-findings
outputs.desc: Buffer overflow and memory corruption vulnerabilities found

outputs.name: exploit-feasibility
outputs.desc: Assessment of exploitability for each finding

process: Disassemble the firmware and identify functions using unsafe string/memory operations
Fuzz network-facing and serial input parsers with malformed input
Monitor for crashes using debug interfaces or watchdog resets
Assess whether stack canaries, ASLR, or NX are present and effective

steps.description: Test the bootloader for insecure boot, firmware downgrade, and persistent backdoor installation.

outputs.name: bootloader-findings
outputs.desc: Bootloader security weaknesses found

outputs.name: persistent-access-paths
outputs.desc: Methods for achieving persistent unauthorized access

process: Determine if secure boot is enabled and verify the full chain of trust
Attempt to interrupt the boot process and access a bootloader shell
Test whether unsigned or modified firmware can be loaded
Check for firmware downgrade protections (anti-rollback fuses or counters)

steps.description: Test radio frequency interfaces (Bluetooth, Zigbee, LoRa, Wi-Fi, cellular) for pairing abuse, replay, and injection.

outputs.name: rf-findings
outputs.desc: Wireless interface vulnerabilities found

outputs.name: rf-attack-surface-map
outputs.desc: Map of wireless protocols and their exposure

process: Enumerate active wireless interfaces and their configurations
Test Bluetooth pairing for PIN bypass, MITM, and unauthorized reconnection
Capture and replay wireless packets to test for replay attack resistance
Test for command injection through wireless protocol payloads

steps.description: Analyze power consumption, electromagnetic emissions, or timing for side-channel information leakage.

inputs.name: overflow-findings
inputs.desc: Known vulnerabilities for targeted side-channel testing

outputs.name: side-channel-findings
outputs.desc: Side-channel leakage paths identified

outputs.name: key-extraction-feasibility
outputs.desc: Whether cryptographic keys can be extracted via side channels

process: Measure power consumption during cryptographic operations with an oscilloscope
Perform simple power analysis (SPA) and differential power analysis (DPA) on captured traces
Test for timing differences that leak information about key material or branching
Assess whether countermeasures (masking, constant-time code) are present

steps.description: Review memory protection configuration: MPU regions, flash read protection, and secure enclaves.

outputs.name: memory-protection-findings
outputs.desc: Memory protection misconfigurations found

outputs.name: data-at-rest-exposure
outputs.desc: Sensitive data accessible through memory read

process: Check MPU or MMU configuration for proper region isolation
Test flash read protection level and whether it can be bypassed through debug interfaces
Check for secure enclave or TrustZone configuration and its effectiveness
Attempt to read sensitive memory regions (keys, credentials) through available interfaces

steps.description: Compile all embedded systems security findings into a final assessment report.

outputs.name: embedded-security-report
outputs.desc: Full embedded systems security assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-priority-list
outputs.desc: Prioritized remediation for hardware and firmware

process: Aggregate findings across debug, firmware, boot, wireless, side-channel, and memory
Score each finding considering physical access requirements and remote exploitability
Write remediation guidance covering both hardware revision and firmware updates
Produce the final report with attack tree diagrams and remediation timeline

description: Assess compliance gaps against a security framework (NIST CSF, SOC2, ISO 27001): control mapping, gap identification, risk prioritization, effort estimation, owner assignment, and remediation roadmap.

steps.description: Map existing security controls to the target framework requirements.

inputs.name: target-framework
inputs.desc: The compliance framework to assess against (NIST CSF, SOC2, ISO 27001)

inputs.name: existing-controls-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of current security controls, policies, and procedures

outputs.name: control-mapping
outputs.desc: Mapping of existing controls to framework requirements

outputs.name: coverage-summary
outputs.desc: Percentage of framework requirements covered by existing controls

process: Decompose the target framework into individual control requirements
For each requirement, identify existing controls that address it (full, partial, or none)
Document the evidence supporting each control mapping
Compute coverage percentages by domain and overall

steps.description: Identify missing or partially implemented controls and classify the gap type.

outputs.name: gap-inventory
outputs.desc: All identified gaps with classification (missing, partial, ineffective)

outputs.name: gap-evidence-list
outputs.desc: Evidence or lack thereof for each gap

process: Flag all requirements with no mapped control as 'missing'
Flag requirements with partial coverage and document what is incomplete
Identify controls that exist on paper but are not operationally effective
Classify each gap by type: policy, process, technology, or people

steps.description: Prioritize compliance gaps by risk to the business and audit timeline.

outputs.name: prioritized-gap-list
outputs.desc: Gaps ranked by risk and audit urgency

outputs.name: risk-heat-map
outputs.desc: Visual heat map of gap risk by framework domain

process: Score each gap by likelihood of exploitation and business impact if exploited
Factor in audit timeline: gaps that will be tested first get higher priority
Consider regulatory penalties and contractual obligations tied to each requirement
Rank the gaps into critical, high, medium, and low priority tiers

steps.description: Estimate the effort, cost, and timeline to remediate each compliance gap.

outputs.name: effort-estimates
outputs.desc: Effort, cost, and timeline estimates per gap

outputs.name: quick-win-list
outputs.desc: Gaps that can be closed quickly with minimal effort

process: For each gap, determine whether it requires a new control or an extension of an existing one
Estimate person-hours, tooling costs, and elapsed time for each remediation
Identify dependencies between remediation items
Flag quick wins (high-priority gaps with low effort) for immediate action

steps.description: Assign an accountable owner to each compliance gap based on organizational structure and expertise.

outputs.name: ownership-assignments
outputs.desc: Each gap assigned to an accountable owner

outputs.name: capacity-conflicts
outputs.desc: Teams or individuals overloaded with gap remediation

process: Match each gap to the team that owns the relevant system or process
Assign a single accountable owner (not just a team) for each gap
Check for capacity conflicts where one team has too many critical gaps
Escalate capacity conflicts to management for resource allocation decisions

steps.description: Build a phased remediation roadmap with milestones aligned to the audit or certification timeline.

inputs.name: quick-win-list
inputs.desc: Quick wins for the first phase

outputs.name: remediation-roadmap
outputs.desc: Phased roadmap with milestones and deadlines

outputs.name: milestone-tracker
outputs.desc: Tracking document for roadmap progress

process: Group remediation items into phases (immediate, 30-day, 60-day, 90-day)
Place quick wins in the first phase for early momentum
Align phase deadlines with audit or certification milestones
Build dependency chains so blocking items are scheduled before their dependents

steps.description: Compile the full compliance gap analysis into a board-ready report.

outputs.name: compliance-gap-report
outputs.desc: Full compliance gap analysis report

outputs.name: executive-summary
outputs.desc: One-page executive summary for board presentation

process: Write the executive summary with overall compliance posture and top risks
Include the control mapping with coverage percentages by domain
Attach the remediation roadmap with ownership and timeline
Produce the final report with appendices for detailed evidence and gap descriptions
